title: Proteomic insight into alkane and 2-ketone degradation by Acinetobacter guillouiae FS11
projectDescription: Characterization of a commercial polyethylene (average Mw~4000, average Mn~1700) revealed the presence of low Mw alkanes and 2-ketones in the material. Based on gas-chromatography mass-spectrometry analyses, Acinetobacter guillouiae FS11 is able to metabolize these compounds. Proteomic analyses revealed the high abundance of enzymes involved in the alkane degradation pathway, as well as multiple flavin-containing monooxygenases (FMOs; putative Baeyer-Villiger monooxygenases), which may be utilized in the degradation of PE-derived compounds.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Acinetobacter guillouiae FS11 was grown using the commercial PE, triacontane and sodium succinate, and biofilm and planktonic cells were collected mid-exponential phase. Cells were lysed, and proteins were precipitated overnight using 12.5% ice-cold TCA. Proteins were digested using the S-Trap™ mini spin column digestion protocol (ProtiFi, USA)  according to manufacturers protocol, reducing with 20 mM DTT and alkylating with 40 mM IAA.  Proteins were digested using a 1:25 (wt:wt) trypsin to protein ratio. Peptides were analyzed on a nanoLC-MS/MS system (Bruker) using DDA PASEF mode.
dataProcessingProtocol: Raw mass spectrometry files were analyzed by the software FragPipe using the annotated FS11 genome as a sample specific database. Carbamidomethylation, and methionine oxidation and protein N-terminal modification were used as a fixed and variable modification, respectively. Trypsin was used as digestive enzyme, with one missed cleavage allowed, and all other paramaters were standard.

quantificationMethods.name: MS1 intensity based label-free quantification method

references.referenceLine: Sandholm RM, Boehlich GJ, Dahl Ø, Chowreddy RR, Stepnov A, Vaaje-Kolstad G, La Rosa SL. Microbial degradation of a widely used model polyethylene is restricted to medium- and long-chain alkanes and their oxidized derivatives. ISME J. 2025 19(1):wraf276
